title: Volcanic Eruption Columns, Ash Plumes and Pyroclastic Density Currents: Rise, Dispersal and Runout Budgets Against Energy and Density Bounds

lessons.title: Lesson 1 — Settle in.
paragraphs: Welcome in. I am Professor Chidi Adeleke, and this is Volcanic Eruption Columns, Ash Plumes and Pyroclastic Density Currents: Rise, Dispersal and Runout Budgets Against Energy and Density Bounds. This is lesson 1 of 1 in the full thirty-minute build of this class. In this lesson we take the class's own material in order — nothing here is imported, and nothing is asked later that is not taught here first. We begin here: Settle in.

Settle in. I am Professor Chidi Adeleke, and this is Volcanic Eruption Columns, Ash Plumes and Pyroclastic Density Currents: Rise, Dispersal and Runout Budgets Against Energy and Density Bounds. This class is built on real papers — deposited, citable work. I will present each paper and what it reports; that presentation is the lesson. At the end I will ask you questions on what was taught here — nothing else.
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

'Calbuco 2015: Stratospheric Injection Fraction, Sulphur Loading and Transcontinental Ash Transport Times'. Its stated result: Headline result: plume height km = 23; tropopause height km = 12; stratospheric overshoot km = 11; settling 20um m s = 0.0327; fall time 20um days = 6.371; fall time 10um days = 25.49
Now we go one step further into the material.

'El Chichon 1982: Inverting Column Height into a Mass Eruption Rate and Erupted Volume'. Its stated result: Headline result: column height km = 21; volume flux m3 s = 1.759e+04; mass eruption rate kg s = 4.397e+07; phase duration h = 9; erupted volume DRE km3 = 0.5698; erupted volume bulk km3 = 1.254
The next piece is where this starts to come together.

'Etna 2021: Lava-Fountain Ballistics, Gas Expansion Velocity and Column Loading During the Paroxysms'. Its stated result: Headline result: gas mass fraction = 0.02; magma temperature K = 1400; vent pressure MPa = 8; gas expansion velocity m s = 350.1; fountain height m = 3437; fountain height if drag free m = 6249
Listen carefully here — this piece carries weight in the questions later.

'Eyjafjallajokull 2010: Settling Velocities, Fall Times and Wind Transport Distances for Fine Ash'. Its stated result: Headline result: release height m = 9000; wind speed m s = 12; particle density kg m3 = 2300; settling 10um m s = 0.006961; settling 30um m s = 0.06265; settling 100um m s = 0.6961
We take the pieces in order, because each one stands on the last.

'Grimsvotn 2011: Umbrella-Cloud Spreading as a Buoyancy-Driven Gravity Current'. Its stated result: Headline result: reduced gravity m s2 = 0.35; volume flux into umbrella m3 s = 2e+05; radius at 1h km = 8.316; radius at 6h km = 31.88; radius at 12h km = 53.61; radius at 24h km = 90.17
Stay with me, because the next piece builds directly on that one.

'Hunga Tonga 2022: Plume Overshoot to the Mesosphere and Umbrella Growth at Record Height'. Its stated result: Headline result: neutral buoyancy height km = 31; maximum height km = 57; overshoot thickness km = 26; ballistic overshoot speed m s = 714.2; reduced gravity m s2 = 0.22; volume flux m3 s = 8e+05
Here is the next piece of the material, in the order the class presents it.

Now my worked example — this class's set problem, worked in full. The problem: Take the paper “Calbuco 2015: Stratospheric Injection Fraction, Sulphur Loading and Transcontinental Ash Transport Times”. Its stated result is: Headline result: plume height km = 23; tropopause height km = 12; stratospheric overshoot km = 11; settling 20um m s = 0.0327; fall time 20um days = 6.371; fall time 10um days = 25.49 (a) Restate the claim in your own words. (b) Name one observation or computation that could prove it wrong. The worked answer: A strong answer restates the claim without borrowing the paper’s wording, then names a test the paper itself would accept — here, the natural test is to recompute or re-measure the headline quantity in the stated result and check it against the paper’s own number, under the paper’s own stated assumptions.

Let us gather what this lesson taught, in order: Settle in; 'Calbuco 2015: Stratospheric Injection Fraction, Sulphur Loading and Transcontinental Ash Transport Times'; 'El Chichon 1982: Inverting Column Height into a Mass Eruption Rate and Erupted Volume'; 'Etna 2021: Lava-Fountain Ballistics, Gas Expansion Velocity and Column Loading During the Paroxysms'; 'Eyjafjallajokull 2010: Settling Velocities, Fall Times and Wind Transport Distances for Fine Ash'; 'Grimsvotn 2011: Umbrella-Cloud Spreading as a Buoyancy-Driven Gravity Current'. Those are the pieces — hold them in that order, because the questions follow the same road.

That is the lesson, whole. Below it are the questions — every one of them drawn from what was just taught, and nothing else. The full text of this lesson stays open beside the questions, and going back to read a piece again is learning, not cheating. When you are ready, begin.

questions.teach: Think back to the lesson — the paper 'Calbuco 2015: Stratospheric Injection Fraction, Sulphur Loading and Transcontinental Ash Transport Times'. The result it reported gives a value for plume height km, and that value is what this question asks for.
questions.teach2: Here is the exact passage from the lesson again: 'Calbuco 2015: Stratospheric Injection Fraction, Sulphur Loading and Transcontinental Ash Transport Times'. Find plume height km in that row; the value beside it is the one this question asks for. Say it in figures, any honest form: as printed, rounded, or written out in full.
questions.walk: Walk it through with me, step by step. (1) In the lesson, the paper 'Calbuco 2015: Stratospheric Injection Fraction, Sulphur Loading and Transcontinental Ash Transport Times' stated its result. (2) That result pairs names with values: plume height km = 23; tropopause height km = 12; stratospheric overshoot km = 11. (3) This question asks for the value paired with plume height km. (4) In that row, plume height km stands beside 23 — so the answer the lesson gives is 23. Now it is yours: say that value, in any honest form.
questions.q: In the lesson, the paper 'Calbuco 2015: Stratospheric Injection Fraction, Sulphur Loading and Transcontinental Ash Transport Times' reported a number for plume height km. What number did it report?
questions.why: You are doing this because a number you can produce from memory — and defend — is worth ten you have only seen glide past.
